schemes.official_name: Industry-sponsored senior capstone design projects (Yale School of Engineering)
schemes.module_code: e.g. MENG 4137L/4138L (Mechanical Engineering capstone, per search summary)
schemes.description: Sponsored capstone projects in the ABET-accredited engineering degree: teams of three to four students design, build, test and refine a functional prototype for a sponsoring organisation over Fall and the first half of Spring, ending in a Sponsored Projects Symposium where sponsors judge group presentations. Sponsors issue a request for proposal, fund all expenses and name a project contact who meets students regularly.
schemes.admin_host: Yale School of Engineering & Applied Science
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Capstone is the final academic requirement for undergraduate students in the ABET-accredited programme; Special Projects open to juniors/seniors.
schemes.credit_assessment: Credit not stated on the page fetched.
schemes.duration: Fall and first half of Spring semester
schemes.delivery_format: Team design-build project with sponsor contact; end-of-year symposium
schemes.project_evidence: Projects 'Lead to comprehensive design and development of a functional prototype' [1].
schemes.group_evidence: Capstone teams are 'groups of three to four students' [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Sponsors issue RFPs, cover expenses, provide a project contact who meets students regularly, judge group presentations at the symposium and receive a final written report [1].
schemes.partner_role: Sponsor/client: sets project, funds, mentors via contact, judges, receives report
schemes.named_partners: ASML (search summary of a Yale news item; undated, not opened)
schemes.deliverable: Functional prototype (retained by students/university) and final written report to sponsor
schemes.unresolved: Page is undated; no dated 2025/26 sponsor list or symposium found. Not shown whether every department's capstone is externally sponsored (the page describes sponsored projects specifically); sponsor type described as industry.

profile_md: Yale's verified provision is distributed across professional schools and one undergraduate programme, with no central or university-wide client-project route found. The strongest curricular routes are the School of Engineering's sponsored senior capstone (teams of three to four building a prototype for a funding sponsor over about 1.5 semesters, judged at a symposium), compulsory within the ABET engineering degree, and the Jackson School of Global Affairs capstone (an optional alternative to the senior thesis: a fall-semester policy project for an external client, such as UNDP's Crisis Bureau and Global Fashion Agenda in Fall 2025, in courses of up to 10 students). At SOM, Discovery Projects (6 credits, application-only) has teams advising affiliate companies, while the student-run Golub Capital Consulting Fellows runs year-long team projects with New Haven nonprofits and public bodies, with dated 2025/26 evidence but extracurricular status. Further team-and-client courses sit in the School of the Environment, Public Health and SOM Global Social Entrepreneurship, but their listings are undated. The legacy Tsai CITY Accelerator is excluded because ventures are student-owned. Uncertain: current-year delivery for most listings, credit and deliverables, and the sponsor share of all engineering capstones.
gaps: Most course listings (YSE, YSPH, SOM GSE, Engineering sponsored capstone, SOM Discovery Projects) are undated, so current delivery is unconfirmed. Jackson capstone group size and clients rest on search-index extracts because the FAQ returned 404 to WebFetch and the Fall 2025 page body did not render. Credits and deliverables not retrieved for several routes. Not researched: further SOM/YSE courses, Architecture, Drama/Art, Divinity, Nursing, Computer Science and Statistics & Data Science capstones, YSE ENV 965 and ENV 985b detail, Yale College humanities departments; further departmental instances likely exist. Reduced-depth mode (about 12 searches).
